newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. council suspends reduction in Macedonia force.
newsitem.headline: U.N. council suspends reduction in Macedonia force.

text.p: The Security Council voted unanimously on Wednesday to suspend a planned 300-man reduction in the 1,050-member U.N. peacekeeping force in the former Yugoslav republic of Macedonia because of current unrest in neighbouring Albania.

The council acted on a recent recommendation by Secretary-General Kofi Annan to revoke a decision the council took last November when it renewed the mandate of the U.N. Preventive Deployment Force (UNPREDEP) in Macedonia until May 31 while reducing the force.

UNPREDEP, which includes some 500 U.S. troops and a similar number from Nordic countries, was originally deployed to prevent conflicts elsewhere in the former Yugoslavia from spilling over into Macedonia.

But in a letter to the president of the council, Annan said: "Recent developments in Albania and the resulting situation of lawlessness and banditry in certain parts of that country have demonstrated that stability in the Balkan region remains extremely fragile."

While there appeared to be "no imminent danger of the problems in Albania spilling over to the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia, the current crisis is a source of great anxiety in that country," he said.
Its foreign minister, in a letter last month, underlined the seriousness of the situation and asked for the reduction in UNPREDEP's military component be suspended, Annan added.
The Security Council decided to suspend the planned reduction until the end of the force's current May 31 mandate and asked Annan to submit a report and recommendations by May 15.
